description: Vector Component Preset Library — Generic robotic building blocks with realistic physical constants for sim-ready model generation.

system_instruction.role: You are Vector's AI design engine. When constructing or editing a robot model, you MUST compose it exclusively from these generic component primitives. Never hallucinate arbitrary masses, dimensions, or inertia values. Instead, select the closest matching preset, use its physical constants, and calculate derived properties (total mass, CoM, inertia tensors) from the assembled set. Use mounting_logic fields to validate that parts interface correctly — e.g., an axial_shaft actuator connects to a hub_bore transmission element, not directly to a face_mount sensor. When the user's request is ambiguous, prefer the smallest component that meets the torque/payload/sensing requirement.

mass_stability_logic.description: How the AI should calculate total mass and assess static stability from selected primitives.
steps: 1. Sum mass_kg of every selected component to get total_mass.
2. For each component, compute its center-of-mass (CoM) position in the world frame using the kinematic chain transforms (joint origins).
3. Compute the composite CoM: weighted average of all component CoM positions (sum(m_i * p_i) / total_mass).

4. For each component, compute its inertia tensor about its own CoM using the bounding_box_mm and inertia_primitive shape. Use standard uniform-density formulas: Box I_xx = m/12*(h^2+d^2), Cylinder I_xx = m/12*(3r^2+h^2), Sphere I_xx = 2/5*m*r^2.
5. Use the parallel-axis theorem to shift each component's inertia tensor to the composite CoM frame.
6. Sum all shifted tensors to get the robot's composite inertia tensor.

7. For static stability: project the composite CoM onto the ground plane. Check that it falls within the convex hull of the ground contact points (support polygon). Margin = minimum distance from projected CoM to nearest polygon edge.
8. For tip-over resistance: compute the minimum torque about each support polygon edge that gravity exerts. If any edge torque is negative, the robot is statically unstable in that configuration.

9. Flag warnings when: (a) total_mass exceeds sum of all actuator payload capacities, (b) CoM height / support polygon width ratio > 3.0, (c) any joint torque requirement exceeds the selected actuator's max_torque_nm by >10%.

mounting_validation: axial_shaft ↔ hub_bore: actuator output shaft inserts into transmission bore (coaxial alignment required).
face_mount ↔ face_mount: bolt-circle pattern, flanged connection (planar alignment, concentric bolt holes).
side_rail_mount ↔ rail_slot: component slides onto extrusion rail T-slot and clamps.
bracket_mount ↔ bracket_mount: L-bracket or U-bracket with through-holes.
tool_changer_master ↔ tool_changer_slave: standardized quick-change plate interface.
press_fit ↔ bore: bearing/bushing pressed into housing bore.

components.name: L-Bracket (90-degree)
components.description: Generic aluminum L-bracket for right-angle structural joints. 3.2mm thick plate (8% of bracket size). Geometry: plate in XY plane with top face at Z=+1.6mm, wall on the -X side rising to Z=+38.4mm. Authors three planar connectors that disambiguate the two distinct mounting surfaces — the legacy default top at +Z/Z=+20 is geometrically invalid (no plate face lives there; bbox corner is empty air), so attach_face:"top" routed via the bbox path historically caused P1 rotation errors (camera / component mounted via 'top' landed with its normal along wrong axis). The authored plate_top / wall_inner / wall_outer give exact pose targets: plate_top for components sitting on the horizontal plate, wall_inner for components facing into the L concave side, wall_outer for components facing out from the back of the wall.

components.name: U-Bracket (Servo Horn)

components.name: Servo Coupler Disc (25T)
components.description: Thin aluminum hub with 25-tooth splined bore on one side and a bolt ring on the other. Couples a servo's rotating shaft to a rigid child bracket/link. Used by the auto-repair pass to resolve shaft-to-mount-face port mismatches. Modeled on goBILDA 1908 series servo hub. Authors shaft_hole (cylindrical, on -Z face with axis -Z, 8mm nominal bore) so a concentric mate against a servo's +Z shaft_out is already-antiparallel — coupler stays upright, bolt-ring side (+Z) faces upward so a child bracket mounts correctly. Also authors top_face (planar, +Z) as a named handle for that bolt-ring side.

components.name: 2-DOF Hip Housing (Compound)
components.description: Single rigid housing containing both abduction and pitch servos for a quadruped leg. Replaces the traditional shaft-bracket-shaft-bracket stack with one integrated unit.
